about: Every name the guide shows to a person comes from this list. Keep the term in English in every conversation language and explain it the first time it appears. `avoid` lists words that must not replace the term in plugin text.

trust.summary: Only a search summary of the source was read.
trust.practice: Widely used in the trade; no single source traced.
trust.unchecked: A named standard recalled from memory; not yet re-read for this list.
trust.coined: Named in this project or by its owner. Not an industry term.

inherited_from: Rows marked inherited carry the trust level recorded in the owner's architecture note of 2026-11-09; they were not re-read for this list.

terms.meaning: The smallest named design decisions: a colour, a spacing step, a type size.
terms.source: W3C Design Tokens Community Group, Technical Reports 2025.10

terms.meaning: Three layers of tokens: primitive (raw values), semantic (roles), component (bound to one component). The token format does not define them; teams choose.
The tier that holds design tokens and the rules for colour, typography, spacing, shape, elevation, motion, iconography and layout.
terms.source: Common practice (Material Design, Atlassian, Primer use it as a top-level section)

terms.meaning: One set of token values for one identity or mode. The structure of the tokens stays the same across themes.
The single colour a whole palette is derived from. Also called source color.
The steps of one hue from light to dark that roles pick from.
What a colour is for (primary, on-primary, surface, outline), as opposed to which colour it is.
The luminance ratio between text or a control and what is behind it. The threshold depends on the conformance level.
The smallest area a pointer control may offer.
The accessibility level a product commits to: A, AA or AAA.
The fixed set of type sizes, each a step from the one before.
The distance between baselines of consecutive lines. Typographers call it leading.
The uniform space added between characters. Typographers call it tracking.
The length of a line of running text, counted in characters.
The fixed set of distances, usually multiples of one base unit.
The corner treatment of surfaces and controls, set as a corner radius scale.
terms.source: Common practice (Material Design names the section Shape)

terms.meaning: How far a surface sits above another, shown by shadow or tone.
The durations and easing curves of transitions, and when a transition is allowed.
How tightly controls and rows are packed, as a named setting rather than per-component sizes.
Columns, gutters and margins that place content, with breakpoints where the arrangement changes.
The icon set and its drawing rules: grid, keylines, stroke weight.
A deliberate departure from the computed value because the eye reads the computed one as wrong. Recorded with its reason.
terms.source: Common practice in type and icon design

terms.meaning: Components from the smallest to larger groups. A description of size, not a folder layout.
Page-level objects that place components in a layout and state the structure of the content.
Templates filled with real content.
The components and conventions shared by the whole organisation.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: Compositions specific to one product. Outside the core, still built on its tokens.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: One-off pieces used in a single place. They need a reason and an expiry.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: A recipe that has proved its worth moves into the core.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: The named parts of a component.
One of a closed set of looks or purposes a component offers.
What a component or a view shows because of a condition: hover, focus, pressed, disabled, selected for a control; loading, empty, error for a view.
A named place in a component that takes content.
Components that supply behaviour and accessibility with no styling.
The expected keyboard and screen-reader behaviour of a widget such as a dialog, a combobox or tabs.
Repeatable answers to a recurring task: saving, notifying, waiting, failing, being empty, searching, filtering.
What a view shows when there is nothing yet, with the first action to take.
What a view shows while content is on its way, usually a skeleton of the coming content.
What a view shows when a request failed, with what failed and how to retry.
An action that removes something and cannot be undone. It asks for confirmation and names the thing.
The rules for words: voice and tone, button labels, error sentences, formats.
Voice is the constant character of the writing; tone is how it shifts with the situation.
Language, and the formats of numbers, dates and currency for a locale.
The channel that delivers component code: a JSON index where each item lists its files and dependencies, installed into the project by a command.
The machine-readable index of components: options, variants, defaults.
A real build chosen as the model to copy.
The opinionated, supported way. Leaving it is allowed and unsupported.
terms.source: Spotify Engineering, How we use Golden Paths

terms.meaning: Shape the types so that a wrong state cannot be written.
Static checks that reject values and structures outside the system.
Comparing rendered screens against approved images.
Who may change the system, how changes are reviewed, and how adoption is tracked. Includes the contribution model.
The share of the product built from the system's components, and the count of detached variants.
A short page that states one decision, its context and its consequences.
Shared test tools: test templates, readiness waits, break-it checks.
Five rungs for how firmly a decision is held, from cannot-be-written-wrong down to written guidance, plus design judgment.
Decisions with an automated check that can fail, divided by all decisions.
